title: feat: one simple newsletter area that publishes, emails and prints
body:
## What

One simple **Newsletters** area for nonprofit staff: write once, then publish to the website, email subscribers, and print/save a two-page PDF. Newspack Newsletters, The Newsletter Plugin and Print My Blog become hidden engines (visible only to `opn_manage_newsletter_engines`, i.e. network administrators).

## Changes

- **Menu**: All newsletters (website + email status per issue, copy-to-new-issue, print, trash), Write a newsletter, Subscribers, Settings. Bare Newspack list and engine screens redirect for non-engine users.
- **Sending** (`includes/delivery.php`): test email to the author and campaigns through The Newsletter Plugin (confirmed subscribers, optional lists, personal unsubscribe tag, first batch immediately). Duplicate sends need explicit confirmation; status reads "Emailed to N subscribers on …".
- **Bug fixed**: sites cloned from a template had an empty Newsletter sender, so every send failed silently while reporting success. Omni falls back to WordPress's From address and listens for `wp_mail_failed`.
- **Editor**: no welcome tour or layout picker; date title replaced with "Month Year Newsletter"; sections labelled in the canvas and locked against removal; Newspack ads/layout/visibility panels, theme template picker and Print My Blog buttons hidden; one "Publish, print & email" panel (website toggle, print, subject, inbox preview text, test, send); Newspack's publish dialog reduced to preview + Publish with a plain explanation.
- **Email**: story and callout groups become separate top-level sections (MJML cannot nest wrappers) with the print palette, yellow headings in dark panels, issue-date band, Arial; inbox preview text generated from the front page.
- **Print**: `?opn_view=print` preview of the two Letter sheets with a live fit check and printing tips; Ctrl+P on the website view switches to the same layout. Print My Blog is no longer required.
- **Subscribers**: add (consent required), paste many, search, unsubscribe, remove, CSV export (formula-safe).
- **Social**: optional Bit Social rule that shares published newsletters to all connected accounts.
- **Filters**: `omni_platform_newsletter_starter_content`, `omni_platform_newsletter_email_colors`.

## Verification

- `composer test` (PHP lint, PSR-12 PHPCS, JS syntax, content contract) — pass.
- Local CEF multisite as a non-administrator role, real browser (Playwright/Chrome), mail captured in Mailpit:
  - Lifecycle suite 40/40: three issues written; test email and 2×4 campaign emails delivered; personal unsubscribe links; stories before contacts; website link in email once published; resend guarded; public pages 200 with 2 sheets and no broken images; 390px mobile has no sideways scroll; print preview "Fits on two pages"; PDFs exactly 2 × 612×792 pt; overflowing issue flagged (not hidden); sections locked; archive lists published issues; no JS errors.
  - Subscribers/settings suite 9/9.

## Rollout

Requires `newsletter` (The Newsletter Plugin) active alongside `newspack-newsletters`. Consumers that pin this package must update their lock.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added a unified newsletter workspace for creating, publishing, and printing newsletters, with subscriber management and configurable settings.
  - Added test and campaign email sending, recipient selection, delivery status, and confirmation before resending.
  - Added optional social sharing and print previews with page-fit status and printing tips.
  - Added web and print views, with links to the site and newsletter archive when available.
  - Added permission-based access to newsletter tools and advanced settings, plus subscriber import, export, and consent controls.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated product and setup guides to describe the newsletter workflow and its requirements.

title: fix: default a blank Newsletter sender to the site's own name and address
body:
## What

A blank Newsletter-plugin sender name made inboxes show only the address; a blank sender address made every send fail. Sites copied from a template inherit whatever the template stored.

Omni now fills blank `sender_name` / `sender_email` when `newsletter_main` is read (`option_newsletter_main` filter): the site's own name and WordPress's From address (which hosting platforms filter to a verified sender). Defaults are computed per site and never stored, so a template can leave them blank and each copy sends as itself. The settings screen reads and saves the stored values only; "From name" says "Leave blank to use your website name". Version 0.2.1.

## Verification

- `composer test` pass.
- Local CEF site with both fields blanked: the Newsletter plugin reports the site name and `wordpress@<site>`, a test email arrived in Mailpit as `CEF Test Chapter <wordpress@…>`, and the stored fields stayed blank.

title: feat: pre-filled first newsletter, archive cards and sign-up box (0.3.0)
body:
## What

Make a new user's first newsletter and the public archive ready without setup.

**Pre-filled first issue.** `starterPatternContent()` is now built from `starterParts()`, filled from the site: tagline as motto, the writer's name (never a bare username) and email, website, giving page (`/donate`, `/give`, `/giving`, `/support-us`), this month, and the site name as kicker and footer. Story spots keep short writing prompts. `omni_platform_newsletter_starter_parts` lets an organization change any part, including two optional photos (attachment IDs), without rebuilding the four-section markup. `omni_platform_newsletter_starter_content` still works. The block pattern is registered only for admin and REST requests, because building it reads the site and user.

**Newsletter archive** (`includes/archive.php`, `archive.css`). For block themes, a plugin template `archive-newspack_nl_cpt` adds:

- a palette-colored masthead;
- issue cards with photo, month badge, title, lead-story summary and "Read this issue";
- pagination;
- a sign-up box using `[omni_newsletter_signup]`, which wraps the Newsletter plugin form.

Themes can override the template.

**Featured image and excerpt fixes.**

- Each issue's first photo becomes its featured image until the writer picks one. This covers cards and social shares.
- `get_the_excerpt` now returns the lead story. Before, it returned the composed page ("Home Newsletters Month Year…").

**Callout and footer link color.** Links in callouts and the printed footer inherit the panel text color, so they no longer show primary-on-dark.

Version 0.3.0.

## Verification

- `composer test` passes. The contract test now asserts that the starter is pre-filled with the site name, tagline, writer and month.
- Local CEF site, logged in as a brand-new CEF Director with no issues:
  - First issue opens with all blocks valid.
  - The email version is generated, and the test email arrives with stories before contacts.
  - The web issue shows the sidebar once.
  - The print view reports "Fits on two pages" with both starter photos.
  - The archive card shows the photo.
- Archive checked at 1440px and 390px widths, with and without issue photos.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a newsletter archive with issue cards, pagination, an empty state, and a signup form.
  * Archive issues can display excerpts and featured images drawn from their content.
  * Starter newsletter content now includes your site details, current date, and writer contact information, with prompts for stories and events.
* **Style**
  * Improved archive card layouts across screen sizes and refined link colors in newsletter callouts and footers.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix: say "1 subscriber" in the send dialog (0.3.1)
body:
## Problem

On a site with one subscriber, the send dialog says "This will email 1 subscribers". `wp_localize_script()` turns the top-level `allCount` into the string `"1"`, and the default `_n()` plural rule (`n === 1`) then picks the plural.

Seen on a new production CEF site.

## Fix

- `assets/editor.js`: convert the counts with `Number()` before calling `_n()`.
- Version 0.3.1 (bumps the editor script's cache-busting version), with a changelog entry.

## Verification

- `node --check assets/editor.js`
- `composer test`: PASS

title: feat: per-issue colour schemes with front/back colours and live editor preview (0.4.0)
body:
## What

Newsletter editors can now choose colours per issue, with different colours for the front and back pages, and see them in the editor while they work. Web, print and email all use the same colours.

- **Colours panel** (`assets/colors.js`, `includes/colors.php`). It has two small page previews, a "Same colours on front and back" toggle, seven ready-made schemes and fine-tuning for each area: page, title, date tags, highlight box, sidebar, motto box, contact box and footer.
  - Each issue stores only the colours the editor changed, in `_omni_platform_newsletter_colors` (sanitised JSON).
  - Anything unchanged follows `palette()`.
  - Text set to "Automatic" is chosen for contrast with its background.
- **Live preview.** The editor canvas is restyled as colours change. Section labels stay readable on dark backgrounds.
- **Rendering.** Each print sheet and web page carries its own CSS variables. Email colours come from `emailColors($post, $side)`, and the `omni_platform_newsletter_email_colors` filter now also receives `$side` and `$post`.
  - Headings inside columns, the motto and the contact box are coloured in email.
  - Colours the author sets on a block are kept.
- **Email freshness.** The email-source hash now includes the colours (`emailSourceHash()`), so a colour change makes a stale email visible. Issues without colours keep the old hash.
- **Paragraph styles.** "Issue label" (a bar) and "Tag over photo" (a tag on the bottom-right of the photo above).
- **Print fixes found while recreating a real newsletter in the editor:**
  - Columns with set widths (25 / 50 / 25) collapsed to zero width. Core's `[style*=flex-basis]{flex-grow:0}` combined with our `flex-basis:0` caused it.
  - Centred and right-aligned paragraphs were forced left.
  - Theme font-size presets (L, XL = 36–42px) overflowed the page. They now scale with the printed text.
  - Blocks added straight onto a page had no side padding.
  - The editor's text-colour highlights showed the browser's yellow `mark` background.
  - A right-aligned date directly above the kicker now shares the kicker's line.
- **Docs.** `docs/newsletter-colours.md` is a step-by-step tutorial with screenshots. `docs/` is excluded from release archives.
- **Version.** 0.4.0.

## Verification (local multisite, cefofidahotopten.com)

- `composer test`: lint, PHPCS and contract test pass.
- I recreated a real two-page autumn newsletter entirely through the editor UI with Playwright, without writing post content directly:
  - copied the last issue from the list;
  - applied the "Autumn sky" scheme to the front and "Autumn harvest" to the back, then fine-tuned;
  - added columns, images (upload and Media Library), highlights, styles and font sizes.
- Print preview of that issue: "Fits on two pages", 2-page PDF, no broken images.
- Regression print checks on an existing issue and the starter issue: both fit on 2 pages with unchanged default colours.
- The email version stays current after colour-only saves (hash matches) and renders with the per-page colours.
- The website view was checked on desktop and phone.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added per-issue color controls, including presets, live previews, and options to link page colors, copy settings, or reset to defaults.
  * Applied issue colors to web, print, and email layouts while preserving author-selected text and label colors.
  * Added paragraph styles for issue labels and photo tags.

* **Improvements**
  * Newsletter copies now retain their color settings.
  * Updated print layouts to better preserve text alignment, column proportions, and font sizing.

* **Documentation**
  * Added a tutorial covering color customization and preparing, previewing, and sharing newsletter issues.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
